Where two runs of the same code differ by one test, the notes name the flaky test (agt-280-requirement-check.test.mjs on 88eba8c3) rather than publishing two totals. ## 532ad560dfcf0a4c · contradiction · medium · ticketed

**Fact:** When and by whom a runner cycle's ticket claim is written: B40 says at pick time by the cycle, run-project.js says in pass two by the driver as its one write, and a claim taken before pass one removes the pick from prime_directive_queue() so the driver names the next row.

**Locations:**
- `runner_cycles:88eba8c3-00e0-408d-ade9-58fe9332d90a` — "FINDING 2, ordering, and it cost one driver round: CLAUDE.md B40 says claim the ticket the moment you pick; scripts/run-project.js makes the claim itself in pass two. I claimed AGT-304 off prime_directive_queue() first, which removed it from the pick path - the driver then offered AGT-340 instead. I released my own claim (holder-guarded), re-ran pass one, and it named AGT-304 again. AGT-183's pick_source="own-claim" repair does not cover this: it re-reads the STORED pick, and by then the stored pick was already the moved-on row."
- `scripts/run-project.js:152` — "PATCH /rest/v1/backlog_items                THE ONE WRITE -- `claimed_by` = the --cycle-id"
- `scripts/run-project.js:331-333` — "Rule B40 has the cycle claim its ticket AT pick time and step 5 runs this driver twice, so between the passes the cycle's OWN claim removes its OWN ticket from the pick path, and the id comparison in `stateDrift` then reads the happy path as tampering."
- `docs/runbooks/runner-cycle.md:2666` — "Rule B40 — Claim a backlog ticket atomically via claimed_by/claimed_at columns at pick time (any session, manual or scheduled); a claim expires after 24h so a dead session can't strand a ticket."
- `docs/runbooks/runner-cycle.md:277` — "**Tickets:** the atomic claim (step 5). A contested claim returns 0 rows → **take the next ticket in the queue**"

**Proposed resolution:** run-project.js pass two should win as the single claim writer in a scheduled cycle (SES-378 slice 2 made its PATCH 'THE ONE WRITE'); runner-cycle.md step 5 should say the cycle takes no hand claim before pass one, and B40's 'at pick time' should be read as the driver's claim for scheduled cycles. B40 itself stands.

**Ruling:** AGT-183 already owns this exact ordering, and the Auditor's claim that it does not is wrong on AGT-183's own text: its fix states both options, including the one this finding proposes. The mechanism repeated this cycle at a cost of one driver round -- the cycle claimed AGT-304 off prime_directive_queue() first, the claim removed it from the pick path, the driver offered AGT-340, and only after releasing its own claim and re-running pass one did AGT-304 come back. scripts/run-project.js:331-333 states the fault in its own comment, and :152 makes the pass-two PATCH 'THE ONE WRITE'. One ordering, two homes that disagree. / Take AGT-183's first option, which is the smaller change and the one that keeps John's rule intact: run-project.js treats 'the state pick is claimed by this same cycle id' as agreement rather than drift, using claimed_by = --cycle-id, data the check already holds. Then runner-cycle.md step 5 says plainly that a scheduled cycle takes no second hand claim before pass one, because the driver's write IS the claim at pick time. CLAUDE.md B40 needs no amendment and gets none: an atomic claim before any work still happens, by one writer, so the rule's substance stands and nothing here is John's to re-decide. (devmanager, 2026-10-05)

**Ruling:** runner_cycles.last_step, ended_at and outcome are each written by a separate prose instruction rather than by the statement that performs the step, so a cycle that completed reads as something else and every reader downstream is misled. Cycle 5a3d7118 shipped v7.0.691 -- verdict 228be707 approve, steps 7a, 8 and the serial tail all in its notes, push 63241a5c..42e98d10 -- while its last_step still reads 'built, waiting for a test slot', against runner-cycle.md:410-417's one-write-per-step-boundary rule and unlike every other shipped row.
